reply_text:
I read this as **borderline**: the quote is on Legg's own blog, but whether it counts as a claim about AI (part 2 of the rule) is unclear, so it should stay out and be logged as borderline.

**1. Is the quote on the page?** Yes, word for word, at the end of the post "Technological themes" on vetta.org, Legg's own blog. The full sentence before it reads: "Well, once you have so much of the economy automated and hooked up together with vast amount of information about anything and everything swirling around, the key leverage point becomes how well you can intelligently process all this in order to control and coordinate things. Thus my pick for the theme from 2025 to 2040 is machine intelligence." The text I fetched shows no posting date. Only the web address gives 2011/01, so I can't confirm the 31 January date the search run reported.

**2. The four parts of the rule:**
- **Part 1 (role): passes, but check it.** DeepMind was co-founded in 2010, so he was a co-founder in January 2011. The ledger already holds his claims from December 2010 and June 2011, so it seems to treat that role as qualifying. Two doubts remain: whether "co-founder" meets the rule's wording ("founder-leader", or "named chief scientist speaking for it"), and whether a startup a few months old was yet building frontier models. He was also writing on a personal blog, not speaking for DeepMind.
- **Part 2 (looks forward and is about AI): borderline.** He predicts which technology will be the main "theme" of new applications over a 15-year span, in a post that also names the PC era and the internet era. That can be read as a forecast about how widely AI will be used. It can also be read as naming an era, without saying AI will do, reach or ship anything specific. Under the rule, a truly borderline case stays out and is logged.
- **Part 3 (has a date): passes.** It gives the years 2025 to 2040.
- **Part 4 (primary source): passes.** The post is his own words.

**Recorded already?** No. None of his 11 recorded claim files is about this.

**If it were admitted anyway:** I see no test an outsider could apply to "the theme is machine intelligence", so it would most likely be marked `unfalsifiable`.
